methods.label: Add the two box paths
methods.explanation: The probability of choosing box A and then drawing red is \(1/3\), and the probability of choosing box B and then drawing red is \(1/6\). Adding gives \(1/2\).
methods.levelReason: The two exhaustive box cases use elementary probability multiplication and addition within the stated elective scope.

methods.label: Recognize six equally likely balls
methods.explanation: Assume each ball in the selected box is equally likely to be drawn. Because the boxes are chosen with equal probability and each contains 3 balls, all 6 individual balls have the same chance of being drawn. Each ball belongs to exactly one box, so counting them covers every possible draw once. There are \(2+1=3\) red balls among these 6 balls. Thus the probability of red is \(3/6=1/2\).
methods.levelReason: Equal box sizes allow a single equally likely outcome count using elementary probability.
